objective: Manage a COPD exacerbation with titrated oxygen and noninvasive ventilation, and recognize when it is failing
secondaryObjectives: Target SpO2 88-92% when a patient is at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure and 94-98% for most others
Interpret a blood gas step by step -- pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate -- and say whether compensation is present

sources.cite: AACN Certification Corporation, PCCN Exam Handbook - Direct Care (July 2026 edition): PCCN Test Plan (exams on and after 2024-02-06), Respiratory
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 for the course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/pccn.ts). Respiratory is 14% of the exam; the plan lists acute respiratory failure and chronic conditions such as COPD, and the testable nursing actions include noninvasive ventilation.

sources.cite: Davidson AC, Banham S, Elliott M, et al. BTS/ICS guideline for the ventilatory management of acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in adults. Thorax 2016;71(Suppl 2):ii1-ii35
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 and again 2026-11-16 in the journal full text on thorax.bmj.com, each through a summarizing fetch with quotes; the 2026-11-16 reading confirmed Rec. 4 and 23 (SaO2 88–92%), 25 (NIV when pH<7.35 and pCO2>6.5 kPa persist despite optimal medical therapy), 30 and 32 (worsening pH and RR change the strategy; consider IMV), all Grade A; the IPAP and pH 7.25 / RR 35 points are narrative text, not graded recommendations (approved for publication November 2015; no newer BTS/ICS version was found). Controlled oxygen to SpO2 88-92% in AECOPD (Grade A); NIV when pH <7.35 and PaCO2 >6.5 kPa (about 49 mm Hg) persist or develop despite optimal medical therapy (Grade A), in practice after about 60 minutes with RR >23; start IPAP about 15 and raise it to 20-30 cm H2O within 10-30 minutes, EPAP at least 3; ABG before and after starting NIV; worsening pH and respiratory rate mean the strategy must change, and invasive ventilation should be considered for persistent or worsening acidosis despite optimized NIV (Grade A); pH <7.25 with RR >35 that persists makes NIV failure likely; care plans should include escalation arrangements from the start.

brief.situation: 02:10 on a progressive care unit. Mrs. Lindqvist in Room 14, 71, admitted from the emergency department at 22:00 with a COPD exacerbation, is hard to keep awake. Her daughter says she "is not herself".
handover: COPD with home SpO2 88-91% on room air. Three nebulizers, prednisone and doxycycline in the emergency department; ipratropium and salbutamol every 4 hours.
Oxygen 4 L by nasal cannula, turned up in the emergency department; SpO2 96%.
02:00 arterial gas (on 4 L): pH 7.29, PaCO2 68 mm Hg, PaO2 82, bicarbonate 32. The night resident has not seen it yet.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Recognize what this is, act and escalate. The therapist, the NIV machine and every gas take time.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. The case ends by 04:40, then a debrief scores what you did.

cues.question: What is happening to Mrs. Lindqvist, why is her SpO2 of 96% not reassuring, and what does she need?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Reads the gas as acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis (pH 7.29, PaCO2 68, bicarbonate 32 partly compensating) causing drowsiness; links it to fatigue in an exacerbation and to oxygen above her 88-92% target.
parts.modelAnswer: pH 7.29 with PaCO2 68 is a respiratory acidosis; a bicarbonate of 32 shows chronic retention with partial compensation, so this is acute-on-chronic hypercapnic failure. The drowsiness and flapping tremor are CO2 narcosis. 96% on 4 L is above her 88-92% target, and too much oxygen can raise the CO2 further.

parts.label: What to do
parts.criteria: Titrates oxygen to 88-92%; escalates with an SBAR asking for NIV (pH below 7.35 and PaCO2 above 49 after medical therapy); agrees an escalation plan before starting; starts IPAP around 15, raises to 20-30 within 30 minutes and fixes leaks; repeats the gas after NIV; recognizes failure (worsening pH and RR) and escalates.
parts.modelAnswer: Bring the oxygen down to a 28% Venturi for 88-92%, call the resident for NIV now, agree her ceiling of care, start IPAP 15 and EPAP 4, raise IPAP to 20 or more within half an hour, refit the mask for leaks, and repeat the gas after an hour. If the pH and breathing rate get worse despite well-run NIV, escalate to critical care for intubation as her plan says.

noProgress.rationale: Two and a half hours of untreated or uncorrected hypercapnic acidosis: the guideline says worsening pH and respiratory rate must change the strategy, so no progress is harm here.

expertPath.text: Assess: drowsy, flapping tremor, accessory muscles. Oxygen down to a 28% Venturi: SpO2 into 88-92%.
SBAR: acute hypercapnic respiratory failure, oxygen too high, now titrated; NIV please, and her escalation plan.
Orders in. Nebulizer. Escalation plan agreed with the resident and with her.
NIV at IPAP 15, EPAP 4; mask refitted for a leak; IPAP 20 within ten minutes.
Gas after an hour on NIV: pH back above 7.35.

intubated.headline: Worsening acidosis
intubated.body: Find when the oxygen came down, when NIV was asked for, the pressures it ran at, and whether the mask leaked or came off.

nivTarget.headline: Titrated, ventilated and checked
nivTarget.body: Oxygen into 88-92%, NIV asked for at once with a plan agreed, pressure raised to 20, the leak fixed and the gas repeated after an hour. That is the expert path.

nivLate.headline: Improving, by a slower route
nivLate.body: She responded, but check the oxygen target, how fast NIV was asked for, whether IPAP reached 20, the leak, and whether her plan was agreed first.

outreachTook.headline: Critical care took over
outreachTook.body: Escalating a failing patient is right. Check whether well-titrated NIV with a good seal would have made it unnecessary.

time_up.headline: 04:40, still acidotic
time_up.body: Without NIV running at an effective pressure, her CO2 stayed high. Worsening pH and breathing rate mean the plan must change.

scoring.modelReasoning: Drowsiness, a flapping tremor and a gas of pH 7.29, PaCO2 68 and bicarbonate 32 on 4 L is acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure in a COPD exacerbation, made worse by oxygen above her target. Bring the oxygen down so SpO2 sits at 88-92%. Medical treatment has already run for hours and the pH is still below 7.35 with PaCO2 above about 49, so call for NIV now and agree her escalation plan before the mask goes on. Start IPAP around 15 with EPAP 4, raise IPAP to 20-30 within 10-30 minutes, fix leaks, and repeat the gas after NIV. If the pH and respiratory rate worsen despite well-run NIV, escalate for invasive ventilation as her plan allows; pH below 7.25 with RR above 35 that persists makes failure likely. Taking the mask off to let her sleep removes the treatment.

failQ.explain: Worsening pH and respiratory rate mean the strategy must change; persistent or worsening acidosis despite optimized NIV calls for invasive ventilation to be considered, and pH below 7.25 with RR above 35 that persists makes failure likely.
